Create the cover illustration for a children's picture book, in a square format. Do not write a title or any other text on it.

Picture: In deep snow on a frosty winter afternoon, the Suitor, in his best clothes and squashed tall hat, with his little travel bag in one hand, knocks politely on the low door of a tiny, lopsided cottage with a sagging, snow-covered turf roof and icicles on the eaves. From the one small window beside the door, three curious faces peek out at him, squashed together: the Farmer, the Farmer's Wife and the Daughter in her new green cap. A low pink sun and lilac-blue shadows.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Suitor: A tall, gangly young man of about eighteen with a round, eager face, apple-pink cheeks, a small blunt nose, bright hopeful blue eyes, a nervous smile and neat butter-blond hair parted in the middle and slicked down flat, with one stubborn tuft sticking up at the back. He wears his best clothes: a slightly too short cinnamon-brown jacket with brass buttons, a white shirt with a little black bow tie, grey striped trousers, polished black boots and a squashed tall black hat, and carries a small brown leather travel bag.
- the Farmer: A big, burly, barrel-chested farmer of about fifty with a broad, ruddy face, a small snub nose, twinkling little blue eyes, bushy brown eyebrows, a shock of unruly brown hair and a long brown beard that splits into two scraggly forks. He wears a faded, patched grey-brown wool jacket whose right sleeve is brand-new, bright lingonberry-red and spotless, while the old left sleeve has a big hole at the elbow, patched brown trousers and worn-out boots.
- the Farmer's Wife: A small, wiry, bustling woman of about forty-five with a narrow, freckled face, a long pointed nose, bright little grey eyes, a busy, pursed mouth and frizzy ginger hair escaping from a patched brown headscarf. She wears a patched mud-brown skirt, a faded grey-blue blouse and a ragged grey shawl. On her right foot is one brand-new, glossy black leather shoe with a big silver buckle; on her left foot, an old, holey grey felt slipper.
- the Daughter: A cheeky girl of about seventeen with a long face, a pointed chin, a turned-up nose, big round brown eyes, pink cheeks, a little rosebud mouth and thick black hair in two short, stiff plaits that stick straight out sideways. She wears a patched, faded brown pinafore dress over a grey blouse, and on her head a brand-new, bright emerald-green knitted cap with a big fluffy white pom-pom, which she is very proud of.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago, in late winter. The poor little farm is a single tiny, lopsided cottage of grey, weathered logs with a sagging, snow-covered turf roof, a crooked chimney, one small window and a low door. Inside is one cramped room with a bare plank floor, a rough little table, a wobbly bench along the wall, two rickety stools and a three-legged stool, a small stone fireplace in the corner with a sooty kettle, and one shelf with two cracked clay bowls. Almost everything is old, grey and patched. The only new things in the house are the farmer's one new sleeve, the wife's one new shoe and the daughter's new cap. The suitor carries a small, square brown leather travel bag with a brass clasp.

This story's season, light and colours: Late winter on a frosty February afternoon: old, crusted snow with lilac-blue shadows, long icicles on the eaves and a low, pink sun. Inside the cottage: warm orange firelight and smoky brown shadows, from which the family's three new things shine out: a bright lingonberry-red sleeve, a glossy black shoe with a silver buckle and an emerald-green cap.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Rounded, friendly shapes and simple, expressive faces with clear emotions, but every character has their own face shape, nose, eyes, hair, build and age exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Base palette of moss green, spruce green, lingonberry red, birch white, fjord teal, honey yellow and warm earth browns, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours. The pictures are the colour plates of a classic printed storybook with warm cream pages, so the lightest tones are warm and creamy, never stark white, and lingonberry red is the accent that comes back in every picture. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:
- No text of any kind: no letters, words, numbers, signatures, captions, speech bubbles or logos.
- Every named character must match their model sheet and description exactly: the same face, hair, colours, clothes and proportions.
- Gentle and safe for young children: no blood, wounds or gore, and no violence in progress. Show danger with mood, posture and distance, never with injury.
- Draw each named character only once.
- Show exactly the number of people, animals and things the description asks for, and no extra people.
- One clear moment that reads at a glance, as a single full-bleed picture with no border, frame or comic panels.
